hardware: Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 (64 vCPUs, 125 GB RAM), virtual machine, no GPU; Docker 29.8 with the whole stack and the load generator on this one machine
stack: gateway (1), enrichers (16), Valkey 9 (append-only file, no snapshots), Qdrant 1.19.1, embeddings BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 on CPU in 16 replicas of 3 threads behind HAProxy (least connections), enrichment heuristic (no decision model), rate limits and queue limit off (bench/compose.yml)
load: k6 1.3.0, 64 virtual users, 30 s per path, paths one after another; enrichers paused during the run and the queue emptied after it

servers.0.4.0: image built from the tag server-v0.4.0 (fingerprint fp1)
servers.0.5.0: image built from main at 4139285 (fingerprint fp2, the privacy-safe demand counters)

haystack: bench/scale/generate.py, seed 11: 34 families of errors with made-up names, one trail per number; numbers 0 to 999,999 (999,999 counted as indexed: one trail is not counted, merged into an identical one or still waiting)
ab_dataset: bench/load/populate.py, 100,002 trails (variants of the nine seed trails), as in the run load-20261001-1921
notes: The A/B run filed the trails with 0.4.0, then started 0.5.0 on the same data: the migration of 100,002 trails took 113 s including the start of the container.
The queue entries that the publish path of k6 left unprocessed were discarded between runs (XTRIM), so each run saw the same data.
